name: the-native-view-toggle-fades-in
description: Turning Native app view on crossfades the surround over the glass instead of painting it in one frame. The fade is a timer on the window, and the two lines it logs - started, then finished a run of ticks later - are what say a run of intermediate frames existed. A snap logs neither.

actions.note: the window paints its tint, which is what the fade needs to fade from
the settings window builds and the route answers

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.settings-rail-item[data-pane="appearance"]'); if (!b) return 'no-pane'; b.click(); return 'clicked'; })()
(() => { const t = document.querySelector('.settings-row[data-key="opaqueSurround"] .settings-row-toggle'); if (!t) return 'no-toggle'; t.click(); return 'clicked'; })()

actions.note: kept for the artifacts: the fade runs 300ms after the write lands, and the write's timing is the file system's

assertions.desc: sanity: the browser window and the settings window

assertions.label: the-setting-landed
assertions.desc: THE CONTROL: the toggle reached the file, so the window had a change to apply.

assertions.label: the-fade-began
assertions.desc: The toggle went through the crossfade, not the instant install.

assertions.label: the-fade-ran-out
assertions.desc: The fade's timer reached its end. Started with no finished would be a fade that hung.

assertions.label: finished-after-started
assertions.desc: The order is the proof of an interval between them.
THE OUTCOME: the sidebar column ended up on the new appearance. Without this the fade lines could come from a fade to nowhere.
assertions.note: Low in the sidebar column, under the rows and clear of the settings window.
